messages:
ashwin: Heads-up — saw two tenant namespaces in eu-west getting routed to hosted GPU pool instead of their Dedicated pool this morning. App latency spiked, and billing jumped.
emily: ugh. any root cause yet? quotas/taints?
maria: on quick look it was a scheduling failure: nodeSelector matched, but Calico IPAM hit regional egress quota so kubelet couldn't finish CNI config. Nodes stayed NotReady and CA removed prewarmed nodes. fallback routing sent requests to hosted to keep apps alive.
jon: can you paste the kubelet/CNI error logs?
ashwin: here's the pod event we saw:
```
Warning FailedToCreatePodSandBox  kubelet  Failed to create pod sandbox: failed to create pod sandbox: failed to setup network for sandbox "...": allocateAddr: region egress quota exceeded
```
maria: stack: dedicated pool had no spare egress capacity because a batch job was doing large model downloads. autoscaler didn't anticipate the transient CNI failures.
emily: so two problems: infra-level egress caps + CA prewarm eviction. How did routing choose hosted over retrying in-region Dedicated?
infra-bot: routing-policy: fallbacks -> hosted when Dedicated pool reports insufficient capacity for 60s. Logged: tenant/alpha reported 3 failed schedules in 45s.
jon: fallback is reasonable for SLA but that defeats data locality and compliance for some tenants.
ashwin: suggestion: change fallback to prefer same-region Dedicated if any node in pool has NotReady but provisioning in progress (i.e., CA scaling up), wait 90s before hosted fallback. Also add CNI backoff and marking of node as "cni-provisioning" so router can make informed decisions.
maria: agree. Also we should label namespaces with `dedicated:strict` when customers require isolation. For those, router must never send to hosted. For others, soft fallback ok.
emily: we also need a quick operational fix: prewarm one extra node per Dedicated pool with a soft-taint and low-priority pods. CA won't evict if soft-taint present.
jon: example label command for namespace:
```
kubectl label namespace tenant-alpha redwood.dedicated=strict
```
ashwin: and CA config tweak (proposal):
```
--scale-down-delay=5m
--expander=priority
--balance-similar-node-groups
```
plus a small change to the controller that marks scaling-in-progress nodes so router can wait.
maria: long term: add a CNI quota-aware prewarm that checks egress/IPAM before adding nodes and throttles large model pulls via a central artifact cache.
emily: concerned about cost if we keep extra prewarm nodes. Proposal: charge soft-prewarm to tenant usage bucket at reduced rate; incentivize them to opt-in. billing team ok with that?
jon: ledger-side it's doable. we'll need a tagging + chargeback story. CC finance.
ashwin: also ran a quick experiment: applied a `prewarm` DaemonSet with `nodeAffinity` to dedicated pool and soft taints. It reduced cold-starts by ~70% during the afternoon spike. Will share metrics.
infra-bot: experiment results uploaded: https://redwood.internal/ops/experiments/1861234567
deploy-bot: rolling change to router fallback timeout to 90s scheduled to canary tonight at 02:00 UTC.
emily: thanks. action items:
- ashwin/maria: PR for router fallback change + node state annotation (due EOD)
- jon: work with finance on prewarm chargeback proposal (due 48h)
- emily: enable namespace label enforcement in policy for strict tenants and add docs
- infra: run prewarm DS for 24h on eu-west to validate
ashwin: I'll open the PR and include the log snippets + CA config patch. ping me for review.
maria: will coordinate with platform on artifact cache prototype.
emily: good thread. let's keep the hosted fallback as safety net but tighten rules so we don't lose locality/compliance silently. :thumbsup:
